etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Italian solo, from Latin sōlus, probably related to se (“himself”).

definitions.definition: (music) A piece of music for one performer.
A job or performance done by one person alone.
(games) A card game similar to whist in which each player plays against the others in turn without a partner
(Gaelic football) An instance of soloing the football.
(music) Of, or relating to, a musical solo.

quote.citation: 1970, Paul McCartney (lyrics and music), “Two of Us”, in Let it Be:
quote.text: Two of us wearing raincoats / Standing solo / In the sun

quote.citation: 1984, “Wake me up before you go-go”, George Michael (lyrics), George Michael (music), performed by Wham!:
quote.text: Wake me up before you go-go / 'Cause I'm not plannin' on going solo

quote.citation: 2024 July 27, Ian Youngs, “Celine Dion makes stirring comeback at Olympics”, in bbc.com‎[1]:
quote.text: The Canadian superstar had been rumoured to be singing a duet with Lady Gaga, but instead went solo on the Eiffel Tower to bring the four-hour event to a stirring climax.

definitions.definition: To perform something in the absence of anyone else.
(Gaelic football) To drop the ball and then toe-kick it upward into the hands.
(slang) To independently perform an action, especially a challenging task.
